findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() disables the $__range guard, causing wrong results for range-variable queries
findings.body: Queries are now mapped through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 299) before the split/no-split decision at line 300. querySupportsSplitting() relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to detect `$__range`, `$__from`, `$__to`, etc. in the raw expression, but after template interpolation those variables have already been substituted with the full dashboard range, so the check never matches. The code comment at line 285-287 explicitly says such queries must not be split because the range variable becomes incorrect per sub-request. Consequence: a query like `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])` now gets split into 1-day chunks with the full range (e.g. `[2d]`) baked in, and each sub-request's start/end truncates the lookback window, so the returned counts differ from the unsplit query — a silent data-correctness regression. The range-variable check must be evaluated against the pre-interpolation expression (or such queries must otherwise stay unsplit). There is also no test covering queries containing $__range after this change, so nothing would catch this.

findings.title: Template variables are applied twice in the shard-splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 52), and then splitQueriesByStreamShard() delegates each sub-request to runSplitQuery() (line 163), which — after this same PR — applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again to those already-interpolated targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). So every query is interpolated at least twice, and once more per additional shard group cycle. A second interpolation pass is not idempotent in general: if a variable's value, a label value, or a log-line filter regex legitimately contains `$` or `${...}` sequences (common in log content), the second pass will re-expand them against template variables, corrupting the query sent to Loki. The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' shows applyTemplateVariables being called 5 times for a single query, but the test mock's replace is trivially idempotent, so this corruption is not covered. The interpolation should happen in exactly one layer, or runSplitQuery should skip interpolation for targets that were already interpolated by the caller.

findings.title: No test that queries with range variables are still excluded from splitting after upfront interpolation
findings.body: The new tests only cover happy-path interpolation of `$__auto` and `$step`. There is no test asserting that a query containing `$__range` (or `$__from`/`$__to`) is still routed to the non-splitting path now that interpolation happens before the querySupportsSplitting() check. Since interpolation substitutes these variables, the existing guard silently stops matching, and without a regression test this data-correctness behavior (documented in the comment on querySupportsSplitting) can break unnoticed — as it appears to in this PR.
